description: What ecoinvent states about one unit of its own flows, read for the merge (#407). Every value here was a bare `conversion_factor` on a row of `ecoinvent-match-overrides.json` until #407; the numbers are unchanged and each now says what quantity it is, which unit it is in, which releases it was checked against and where it came from. Shared by every ecoinvent release the manifests declare, with `by_release` where a release restated a measurement: crude oil was 42.3 MJ/kg in 3.8 and 43.4 from 3.9.1 on, and 3.8's natural gas is per plain cubic metre where later releases are per standard cubic metre. The coal values come from ecoinvent's EF 3.1 implementation workbook, which states no basis, so they are `calorific-value`; crude oil and natural gas carry `heating value, net` on the exchange itself from 3.9 on and are `net-calorific-value`; uranium is fission energy, never a heat of combustion.

primary_source: ecoinvent's EF 3.1 LCIA Implementation workbook, sheet CFs, category `Resource use, fossils`: the factor on the kilogram or cubic-metre flow, which is 1 MJ/MJ times the energy content; the exchange carries no heating value property
statements.comment: The energy-content conversions the retired tables carried (#141), restated as this project's rows with nothing changed: ecoinvent extracts its fossil energy carriers and sea water in kilograms and EF 3.1 publishes the resources in megajoules (or as its own basis), and the factor is the carrier's energy content -- 9.41 MJ/kg brown coal, 18.01 hard coal, 43.4 crude oil, 36.0 natural gas, 560,000 uranium, and sea water's density pairing. Without these the retirement build landed every one of the rows on a kilogram flow of the right substance and EF's fossil-depletion factors, which live on the energy flows, became unreachable from ecoinvent -- the #33 underestimate by a new road. The numbers are the tables' own, read out of the composed 3.8 table before its retirement. Read off ecoinvent's own LCIA implementation workbooks, one per release: `LCIA Implementation v3.8.xlsx`, `3.9.1`, `3.10.1`, `3.11` and `3.12`, `energy resources: non-renewable` under EF v3.0 and EF v3.1. The characterisation factor for a kilogram flow under an indicator defined per megajoule is the energy content, which is why the workbook answers this question at all. The same number in all five releases' workbooks, so the row's factor needs no release of its own. (#162)

(#141) Checked across releases against the three published correspondence tables that ever stated it -- `ecoinvent-3.9.1`, `-3.10.1` and `-3.11` biosphere to EF 3.1 biosphere -- which state the same number in each; 3.12 read 3.11's table and 3.8's was composed. The basis cannot carry a release's revision in any case: it is a density of sea water, a property of the substance and not of any ecoinvent release. (#162)

statements.comment: One of the energy-content family; the full reasoning is on the family's first row above. Stated after an independent review of #336 found the first cut silently dropped the factor for 3.8. (#141) Read off ecoinvent's own LCIA implementation workbooks, one per release: `LCIA Implementation v3.8.xlsx`, `3.9.1`, `3.10.1`, `3.11` and `3.12`, `energy resources: non-renewable` under EF v3.0 and EF v3.1. The characterisation factor for a kilogram flow under an indicator defined per megajoule is the energy content, which is why the workbook answers this question at all. ecoinvent revised this value at 3.9 following Meili et al. (2021) and rebuilt its oil and gas datasets on the new number, so a 3.8 inventory has to be converted with 3.8's figure: converting it with the later one used a heating value that release never had. The line falls exactly between 3.8 and 3.9.1, and of the seven carriers the workbooks state only this one, crude oil and mine off-gas moved -- the coals, peat and uranium cite the older source in every report and did not. (#162) 34.5 MJ per cubic metre in 3.8's workbook and 36.0 per standard cubic metre from 3.9.1 on. The two spellings under `source_unit` and the two factors line up: 3.8 is the release that ships `m3`, and the releases that ship `sm3` are the ones the 36.0 was read from. The sentence that used to stand here said ecoinvent respelled the unit at 3.9 "without restating any amount", and the amount was restated in that very release -- a statement about units standing in for one about releases.
